q: How do I count rooftop solar with net metering in Scope 2?
title: Rooftop solar and net metering in Scope 2
short: Report Scope 2 on the units you imported from the grid, not on the net units your discom bills. Solar you generate and use on site has no Scope 2 emissions. Units you export do not cancel units you import, so never subtract exports from imports when calculating emissions.

sections.h: Read the three numbers on a net-metered bill
ul: Import: units drawn from the grid. This is your Scope 2 activity.
Export: units your solar sent to the grid. These are not deducted for emissions.
Net: import minus export, used for billing. Do not use it for Scope 2.
p: Your total electricity use is import plus the solar you used on site. The solar meter or inverter gives generation; self-consumed solar is generation minus export.

sections.h: Why exports cannot be netted off
p: Scope 2 counts emissions from the electricity you consumed from the grid. Exported solar is electricity someone else uses. The GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance does not allow avoided emissions from exports to reduce your inventory. If you want to show the benefit, report generation and exports separately in a note.

sections.h: Net metering, net billing and gross metering
ul: Net metering: imports and exports are netted for billing only. Scope 2 is still on imports.
Net billing: imports and exports are priced separately. Scope 2 is on imports.
Gross metering: all solar goes to the grid and all your use comes from it. Scope 2 is on all units consumed, because none of your use is self-generated.
p: Which arrangement you have depends on the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, as amended, your state regulator and your connection size. Check your agreement with the discom.

In market-based reporting, self-consumed solar counts as renewable only if you keep its attributes. If you sell renewable energy certificates for that generation, you cannot also claim it. Imports are reported with your supplier or residual factor, or with certificates you hold.

example.title: Worked example: one month with rooftop solar
lines: Import 30,000 kWh, export 8,000 kWh, solar generation 20,000 kWh
Self-consumed solar: 20,000 minus 8,000 = 12,000 kWh; total use 42,000 kWh
Wrong method on net units: 22,000 x 0.710 = 15,620 kg CO2, understated by 5,680 kg

senseible: Senseible reads the import units on an electricity bill and applies the India grid factor of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. Net-metered units are not treated as consumption, and kVAh lines get no factor until kWh is available. It does not read inverter or solar meter data.
